title: Effects of economic growth in Australia
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:12Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-20T12:25:40Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No single bank point covers both the benefits (jobs, incomes, tax for services) and the costs (inflation, inequality, environmental harm) in the brief; the closest cards each cover only one side, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Effects of economic growth in Australia
card: When the economy grows, businesses often need more workers, so more jobs can be created. More jobs and higher wages can lift incomes.
Higher incomes and more spending mean the government can collect more tax. That money can pay for services such as hospitals and schools.
Growth can also push prices up when spending rises faster than the economy can produce. This rise in the general level of prices is inflation.
The gains may not be shared evenly, so the gap between richer and poorer households can widen. Using more land, water and energy can also harm the environment.
draft.remember: Growth can bring jobs, incomes and tax for services, but it can also bring inflation, inequality and harm to the environment.

a.q: A mining town in Western Australia grows quickly. Which is a possible benefit for the people who live there?
opts: A smaller gap between rich and poor
Less pressure on local water supplies
a.why: Growth often means businesses hire more workers, which can lift incomes. The other options are costs or opposite effects: growth can push prices up, widen the income gap and use more water.
a.clue: Think about what businesses need when they produce more.

b.q: Over five years, Australia's economy grows and the government collects more tax. At the same time, the wealthiest households gain far more than the poorest. Which pair of effects is this?
opts: More tax for services, and greater inequality
Harm to the environment, and higher incomes
b.why: More tax collected is a benefit, because it can pay for services. Gains going mostly to wealthier households is inequality. Inflation is a rise in the general level of prices, which the scenario does not describe.
b.clue: Match each part of the scenario to one effect on the card.

b.best: More tax for services, and greater inequality
